page: Microsoft Azure D64pds_v5 is an ARM-based virtual machine belonging to the DPDSv5 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated physical cores powered by an Ampere Altra ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 3.0 GHz. The CPU configuration includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, with a single thread per core. The system is equipped with 208.0 GB of RAM, yielding 3.25 GB of memory per core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of a 2458 GB SSD, and the instance is capable of utilizing Premium Storage. No GPU accelerators are present.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core and memory performance. The server achieves top-tier results in multi-core stress-ng CPU tests and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Memory bandwidth for small cached blocks is highly efficient at 4383.55 GB/sec, and Redis SET operations reach 82.63 million operations per second. Software compilation with Clang and ray tracing benchmarks also fall into the top performance tier. Conversely, single-core performance is a notable tradeoff, with single-threaded bzip3 decompression, Geekbench single-core scores, and text processing benchmarks ranking in the lower tier. Large-block memory bandwidth, static web serving throughput, and LLM inference for small to medium models remain in the average tier.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the D64pds_v5 leverages the ARM64 architecture to deliver high resource density and strong multi-threaded performance per unit of power and hardware cost. The inclusion of a large 2458 GB local SSD reduces the need for external storage attachments for high-throughput local data operations. This server is suited for multi-threaded workloads, software compilation, Redis-based caching layers, and database operations that benefit from dedicated physical cores and local SSD storage, while it is less optimal for single-threaded tasks or large-scale LLM prompt processing.
